name: Bounty: The Smuggler's Mine
description: A gang of goblin ambushers has taken over an abandoned mine on the outskirts of the city, using it to stash stolen goods. The Guild is offering a bounty for clearing them out and retrieving the stolen cargo.

node_01.name: Mine Entrance
node_01.base_description: You stand before the gaping maw of the Smuggler's Mine. A rusted iron sign, long since defaced by claw marks, once read 'Keldrath Co. — Authorized Personnel Only.' The air is damp and thick with the smell of mud and something older, something rotten. Dripping water echoes in the dark. To your left, a collapsed ore cart lies on its side, its wheels stripped. The only way forward is the Main Shaft, a dark tunnel yawning open straight ahead.
node_01.lore_fragment:
### The Smuggler's Mine
Once a legitimate iron mine operated by the Keldrath Company, the Smuggler's Mine was abandoned a decade ago when the veins ran dry. Rumour has it the company's foreman was found dead at the bottom of Shaft Three under mysterious circumstances. Since then, opportunists have used the tunnels as a black-market waypoint, and something older may have moved in long before the goblins arrived.

node_02.name: Main Shaft
node_02.base_description: The main tunnel is wide enough for three men abreast, the walls reinforced with rotten timber beams that groan underfoot. Ancient torches hang in iron brackets, their oil long since spent. A cold draft flows from deeper in — something breathes in the dark below. The path splits ahead: a rusted iron gate, nearly wrenched off its hinges, blocks access to the Storage Bay to the east. To the north, the tunnel continues toward the sounds of distant voices. The Entrance lies back the way you came.
node_02.lore_fragment:
### The Iron Gate
The gate bears the emblem of a coiled serpent biting its own tail — the same sigil found on three other 'abandoned' mine sites across the kingdom. Whatever the Keldrath Company was really doing here, they wanted certain things very well guarded.

node_03.name: Storage Bay
node_03.base_description: The Storage Bay reeks of stolen goods: sacks of grain, crates of weapons, and barrels stamped with Guild insignia that was clearly meant for legitimate merchants. Sloppy handwriting on a wall details crude inventory tallies in what you recognize as Goblin script. Hooks on the wall hold rope, torches, and a set of lockpicks that someone dropped in a hurry. The room is quiet now, but recently disturbed. Clawed boot prints lead back toward the Ambush Chamber. The only exit back is through the broken gate.
node_03.lore_fragment:
### The Stolen Cargo
The Guild markings on the barrels confirm it: three of these shipments were reported hijacked on the King's Road over the past month. Someone organized is running this operation — goblins alone are not capable of this level of logistics. There is a handler deeper in the mine.

node_04.name: Ambush Chamber
node_04.base_description: Torches blaze to life along the walls the instant you step through the threshold — a crude tripwire mechanism. The chamber opens into a wide, low-ceilinged cavern. Crates are stacked into impromptu barricades. A screech rips through the air. Goblin Ambushers melt out of the shadows, blades drawn, yellow eyes gleaming with malice. The exit back to the Main Shaft is behind you. A reinforced door at the far end, marked with a crude skull, leads deeper. But first — you will have to fight.
node_04.lore_fragment:
### The Ambushers
These are no ordinary scavengers. The goblins here are disciplined, organized, and equipped with stolen Guild-issue weapons. Someone trained them. Their leader, a scarred brute the others call 'Skrix,' takes orders from something that hasn't shown its face yet.

node_05.name: The Boss's Den
node_05.base_description: The air here is thick with incense and the acrid tang of alchemy. A crude throne made from smashed crates sits at the centre of the room. Mounted on the wall: a detailed map of the King's Road, with red marks at every ambush site. The floor is scorched in a wide circle — dark ritual markings. On the throne, reclining with contemptuous ease, sits the Mine Boss: a towering cultist in patched iron armour, his eyes reflecting the torchlight with an unnatural orange glow. He smiles when he sees you. He knew you were coming.
node_05.lore_fragment:
### The Mechanized Cult Connection
The ritual circle on the floor matches illustrations in a forbidden text recovered last winter by the Ascendants. The Mine Boss is not just a criminal — he is an acolyte of the Mechanized Cult, siphoning resources to fund something far larger than a smuggling ring. The cult's reach extends deeper into the university's core than anyone suspected.
